text:
Aisha Patel: Hey team — Contrax sent a renewal quote for our usage (invoice CTX-8421) but the numbers look off compared to what Finance has. Quote says $24,000/yr for the Starter bundle (4 seats + 100k API calls) but our actual usage last quarter shows ~250k calls/mo. Can someone help reconcile?

Carlos Nguyen: Can you drop the PDF or a screenshot? If they priced us as a seat-only subscription that'll definitely underspec the API volume.

Aisha Patel: Attached screenshot pasted here: https://files.redwood/procurement/contrax_quote_march.pdf — main line items: Starter $24k/yr, Integration fee $5k one-time, Overages $0.02 per extra call.

Maya Lin: With 250k calls/month avg, that's ~3M calls/yr. At $0.02/call overage that's huge if not covered by bundle. Need to know how they counted "included calls" — is it per-seat or per-org?

Samir (Contrax Sales): Hey Aisha, thanks for flagging. Our Starter includes 100k calls/yr, not per month. The quote assumes a small-footprint seat model. If you plan to use high-volume API, we usually recommend our Scale plan or a committed usage add-on. I can share an updated TCO table.

Aisha Patel: Oof — that's the disconnect. We never agreed to per-year cap that low. Can you ask for a committed-usage rate for 3M calls/yr? Also request a pilot credit for the current quarter (we're mid-run on an eval).

Carlos Nguyen: Per procurement playbook, ask for: 1) committed volume discount (tiered), 2) overage cap per month, 3) 60-day termination rights during pilot, 4) standard SOC2 attestation. Also get an explicit SLA for API availability.

Samir (Contrax Sales): Understood. Draft counter-proposal I can offer now: - Committed 3M calls/yr at $0.006/call = $18k/yr (calls only) - Seats + support = $8k/yr - One-time integration waived as pilot credit - Overage capped at $0.01/call with monthly cap at 15% over commit - 45-day pilot termination. I can get SOC2 cert and add SLA language.

Maya Lin: That first line on $0.006/call looks reasonable compared to $0.02. Can you ask them to make the overage cap explicit in dollars (e.g., max $2k/mo) vs percentage? Easier for budgeting.

Aisha Patel: Also ping Legal: we need payment terms (Net30 vs Net45), and indemnity language. If they insist on Net45 we might need to push for Net30 + early-pay discount.

Carlos Nguyen: I'll prepare the procurement counter-email. Plan: 1) Accept pilot credit + integration waiver 2) Request written committed rate at $0.006/call for 3M calls, add explicit monthly overage cap of $2,000, 3) 60-day termination for pilot, 4) Net30 payment, 5) SLA 99.9%.

OpsBot: Reminder: procurement approvals required for commitments > $10k/yr per the policy doc: https://intra.redwood/procurement/policy — route to Finance and Eng leads.

Aisha Patel: Thanks — Carlos, can you send the email draft here for quick review? I want to include the actual usage CSV excerpt before we send.

Carlos Nguyen: Sure, drafting now. Quick usage snapshot to paste into the thread for the vendor:

```
Month,API calls
2025-11,240000
2025-12,260000
2026-01,250000
```

Carlos Nguyen: Draft subject: "Request for revised committed pricing & pilot credits — Contrax (Redwood Inference)" — will post draft in 15 min.

Samir (Contrax Sales): Appreciate the clarity. If Finance signs the 3M commit we can lock the rate for 12 months and add a clause to renegotiate only if monthly average exceeds 125% of committed volume for 3 consecutive months.

Aisha Patel: Good — sounds like a path forward. Once Carlos posts draft we'll approve and I will escalate to Finance for the >$10k approval.

Carlos Nguyen: Draft posted: https://docs.redwood/contracts/contrax-counter-2026-draft.md — please review quickly and thumbs-up here so I can send.

Maya Lin: Reviewed, +1 on the $2k/mo cap language and adding an explicit clause that integration hours are capped at X for the waived credit.

Aisha Patel: +1. Sending after approval. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
